newsitem.title: USA: US debt futures end up, near 6.75 pct magnet.
newsitem.headline: US debt futures end up, near 6.75 pct magnet.

text.p: U.S. debt futures closed up sharply Friday and near session highs after a steady shortcovering bid and a strong attraction to the 6.75 percent cash yield kept prices aloft for most of the session.
"There has been a shortcovering bid in the market all day long," said a bond futures floor broker.

Funds that sold futures the previous day, helping send September bonds to their lowest level in two weeks, spent the day buying back contracts, said the broker. The persistent bid caused September futures to retrace the prior session's entire down move.

After pushing through resistance at 111-16 late in the morning, prices hovered above the level for the rest of the session. Traders equated the level with the 6.75 percent cash bond yield, which reined in the rally in Treasuries.

Front-month Eurodollar futures moved little by contrast, which traders said reflected the widespread view that the Federal Open Market Committee will leave short-term interest rates unchanged at its two-day meeting beginning Tuesday. December Euros have traded sideways for two weeks.
"Everybody's on hold until they get the meeting out of the way," said a Eurodollar floor broker for a U.S. bank.
The bank trader added that further out on the Eurodollar curve, futures continue to price in the potential for a Fed rate hike toward the end of the year.

Debt futures prices began their recovery overnight in tandem with a rise in the dollar against the yen on receding expectations for a rate hike in Japan after data released there sent mixed signals on the country's economic recovery.
The dollar was at 114.50 yen late in the U.S. trading day.
U.S. stocks also powered ahead, eliminating a potential source of worry for the bond market, debt traders said.
